ety.text: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *ěda, from *(j)ěsti (“to eat”), from Proto-Balto-Slavic *ḗˀstei, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁ed- (“to eat”). Cognates include Ancient Greek ἔδω (édō) (> ἔδεσμα (édesma)), Latin edō (> epulum, ēsca; see also prandium), Sanskrit अत्ति (átti), Lithuanian ė́sti (“to eat (of animals), to swallow, to gobble”), Hittite 𒂊𒀉𒈪 (eidmi, “I eat”), Old English etan (English eat).

tpl.gloss: to eat (of animals), to swallow, to gobble

Perhaps from French élast(ique) + -и́чный (-íčnyj). Omitting several steps, from Ancient Greek ἐλαστός (elastós) (variant of ἐλατός (elatós) < ἐλαύνω (elaúnō)).
